oil.summary: Crude sold off on the day — Brent -1.42% to $89.45, WTI -0.59% to $83.96 — but both benchmarks remain up more than 20% on the month, reflecting the geopolitical risk premium built in since Gulf export disruptions began. The sharpest intraday pain was in products: RBOB cratered 8.02% and Heating Oil fell 5.73%, paradoxically as Goldman Sachs flagged a diesel crunch tied to the lowest global refining activity since the 2020 pandemic. Russia's extension of diesel and gasoline export bans through January 2027 tightened the distillate picture further, while record U.S. refinery runs have so far failed to fill the gap. Iran's continued oil blockade, a drone strike on Egypt's Damietta port gas storage tanker, and a Senate-passed Russia-Iran sanctions bill featuring proposed 500% tariffs keep the geopolitical floor firmly under flat price.
drivers: Russia extends diesel and gasoline export bans to January 31, 2027, deepening the global distillate crunch flagged by Goldman Sachs
Iran maintains Strait of Hormuz oil blockade; US imposes fresh sanctions on Iranian oil tankers; drone strikes Egyptian port infrastructure
Record U.S. refinery runs insufficient to offset global supply gaps; U.S. Senate passes sweeping Russia-Iran sanctions bill with 500% tariff proposals

gas.summary: TTF surged 4.65% on the day to €60.42/MWh, extending a month-long rally of nearly 42% driven by Middle East supply disruptions. The standout headline is QatarEnergy purchasing as many as 33 U.S. LNG spot cargoes this year to fulfil Asian customer commitments after Iran-related conflict damaged Ras Laffan operations — a structural rerouting of Atlantic Basin LNG that tightens European and Asian spot markets simultaneously. A drone strike on a gas storage tanker at Egypt's Damietta port adds further near-term supply vulnerability. Henry Hub, by contrast, drifted only modestly higher (+0.81% to $2.747/MMBtu), remaining under pressure on the month (-16.12%), as U.S. production continues to absorb incremental LNG export demand without acute domestic tightness.
drivers: QatarEnergy buying up to 33 U.S. LNG spot cargoes after Iran war damage to Ras Laffan, tightening global LNG availability
Drone strike on gas storage tanker at Egypt's Damietta port raises additional regional supply disruption risk
TTF-Henry Hub spread widening sharply: TTF +42% on the month vs. Henry Hub -16%, reflecting divergent regional supply-demand balances

power.summary: EU Carbon EUAs slipped 0.55% to $77.26, consolidating after a modest month-on-month gain of 2.52% — muted relative to the volatility seen in underlying fuel markets. TTF's 4.65% daily jump is the dominant input cost driver for gas-fired generation across Europe, with the broader Middle East conflict sustaining upside risk to fuel costs. Iran's ballistic missile strike on American bases in Jordan, reported today as the first such Tehran-initiated attack on U.S. targets, signals escalating conflict dynamics that could further disrupt energy infrastructure. On a structural note, China's coal share in electricity output fell below 50% for the first time on record in H1 2026, a landmark data point for long-run carbon demand trajectories, though it provides little near-term EUA price support.
drivers: TTF +4.65% on the day raises gas-fired generation costs across Europe, indirectly supporting carbon prices at the margin
Iran fires ballistic missiles at U.S. bases in Jordan in a reported first; escalating conflict sustains upside risk to European energy supply and EUA volatility
China's coal share in power generation falls below 50% for the first time in H1 2026, a structural milestone with long-term bearish implications for global carbon intensity
